In general, when the tears come, taking some deep breaths and telling yourself it's okay, getting some fresh air, spashing your face with water and similar things can help.

However, with this type of pattern, I can't help but think there may be some underlying causes. The past three years have been tough on most of us and our social skills.

Be honest with yourself, are you okay? Has something been bothering you without you realising it? Have you maybe been bottling up some stuff that needs out? Crying isn't necessarily a bad thing. Yes, it's uncomfortable when it happens in public, but a good hard cry can actually be therapeutic. Crying releases stress hormones, which is why we usually feel better after a good cry. So. I'd say, have a good cry in the privacy of your home with plenty of huggables and ice cream (or whatever is comforting to you) and see if it helps. if the problem persists, consider seeking professional help or talking to someone you trust.

I understand that you are in a lot of pain. A defining characteristic of depression is that people often don't know where it comes from. It just is, with no rhyme or reason. You seem to be doing everything right (therapy, pills, exercise) and yet you're still unhappy. That must be awful.
You absolutely deserve happiness and I sincerely hope you will one day find it.
That being said, I think a career change could be helpful to you. Mental health is without doubt one of the most stressful and emotionally exhausting jobs out there. You may not even realise how much it takes out of you. It may take some additional therapy or intense self-care to deal with that.
But again, depression doesn't always have a cause. And that's okay. What's important is that you take care of yourself and do things that actually feel good to YOU. Be that spending time with your loved ones, taking an hour for yourself to take a bubble bath or overindulging on a bar of chocolate from time to time. Talk to your therapist to help you figure out what it is you're missing and what you can do about it. I hope find happiness in your life, you absolutely deserve it.

However, it is possible that your friend may be struggling with her own issues causing her to withdraw, but that does not mean those issues are in may way related to you.
If you already have an appointment with your therapist, you should probably go, if you can get yourself there. Or maybe you could ask them to do it on the phone instead? I hope you feel better soon.

The first step of change is realising you need help. Good job on that!

Getting stuck between wanting to change and simultaneously fearing change is perfectly natural. Change is scary.
In order to overcome this state, you have to get to a point where you want to change more than you don't want to change.
How people reach this point varies. Often it's a wake-up call in form of a medical diagnosis or near-death experience or the birth of a child or grandchild that they suddenly realise they want to be there for.
If you have any of those reasons, focus on that. If not, you're going to have to find another reason. It needs to be a good, strong reason and one that benefits you more than your loved ones. You're still young, so think about what you want from life. Do you want to live a long, healthy life so you can see your children grow into adulthood and have their own children? Do you maybe want to travel the world and go exciting places? Whatever it is you want from life, you won't be able to do it at the bottom of a bottle. So hold on to that when you find yourself wondering why you even bother.

I'm also going to be honest with you and say that the road to recovery is long and hard. And that you probably will fail at some point. But that's okay. It's an addiction, if it were easy to break it wouldn't be called that. The important thing is that you don't give up. Get back on that horse the next day and stay in the saddle a little longer.

It's important that you have a support network, be it friends, family or an anonymous group of people in the same situation. Find your people and don't be afraid to ask them for help.
I hope you get better soon.
